# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Pass 23** — through-code on Datasec/NexusAI **RD-245 + RD-155** at `b8068485cc` (2026-09-04 13:5x→14:15, ~20 min; static plus nine runtime probes, all tampering on `git archive` extractions in mktemp scratchpads, target tree untouched and clean at 0 porcelain lines) | 1 | **1.00** | 1.00 | 🔴 **FOUND A BLOCKER UNDER A GREEN GATE IT HAD ITSELF RE-DERIVED — the single strongest argument for this gate that the fleet has produced.** `1504/1504 across 88, jest exit 0` is TRUE, the tester re-ran it, **and F-1 and F-2 are both green under it.** **F-1: RD-245's fix cannot fire on the write path** — `setSetting()` stamps a fresh `_updated_at` on every write so no two consecutive states are byte-identical, making `liveHash === currentHash` UNSATISFIABLE there, while `writeFile()` calls `backupFile()` before every write so every write consumes a slot. **Replayed the incident to BYTE-IDENTICAL outcomes on the fixed and unfixed trees** — the good copy dies on both; `server.js:3798-3804` issues seven consecutive `setSetting()` calls. Builder claims 1 and 2 falsified. **F-3 is the explanation and the keeper: the test models the mutation as raw `fs.writeFileSync`, which consumes NO rotation slot, while the product's `setSetting()` consumes one — five green tests never enter the product's state machine.** A fixture that cannot reach the product's path cannot see the product's defect, written by the person who understood the defect best. **F-2: RD-155 moved the SELECTION, not just the warning** — RD-143 cleared Priority 1 only; it remains a selection gate at `jsonStorage.js:560-563/:575-578/:586-589`, so a `$HOME/data` holding only `{"showSetupGuideOnStartup": false}` now BEATS a directory with real settings. **The builder's asymmetry argument is sound for the warning and unsound at those three call sites, where a false positive ABANDONS the populated directory.** **F-5: the criterion-3 warning fires in 2 of 9 probed states and BOTH are false alarms — 0 correct — 'a `logger.error` that can only ever be wrong.'** **METHOD: it led its NOT-TESTED with the pass's biggest hole and kept two claims apart that a weaker report would have merged — it never read the incident artifacts, so F-1's reconstruction of THAT incident is unproven while F-1's EXPOSURE stands on the measured replay.** Every finding carries its evidence class; four builder claims CONFIRMED including one it independently red-proofed by asking what else the early return skips. **TWO SELF-CORRECTIONS IN THE OPEN: (1) it used `rm -f` ONCE on a symlink in its own scratchpad, broke the standing rule, reported it unprompted and noted the next line (`ln -sfn`) made it unnecessary — NOT penalised; the disclosure is what the scoreboard protects. (2) its criterion-3 probe took THREE oracles before it was right — run 1 contaminated by a constructor that consumed the installed state, run 2 scored against a post-condition that would have produced three bogus MISSED rows it 'would have filed as defects' — and all three scripts are in `evidence/` so the progression is auditable.** |
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Pass 22** — Datasec/NexusAI **S31 item 0** (Kam's conform-both) at `2f3ce7d` (2026-09-04 09:10→09:38, ~28 min; through-code PLUS a real browser on its own `:3191` — first pass in this campaign with rendered evidence) | 1 | **1.00** | 1.00 | **All six builder claims survived falsification, and the separator was confirmed BY CODEPOINT at the render** — rendered UTF-8 byte-identical to the mock's line 117, only non-ASCII being U+2013 and U+00B7. *

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.
